title: Raconter une expérience et en tirer un commentaire mesuré
summary: Connect background, turning points and prior events, then draw a useful lesson without turning one experience into a universal claim.
objectives: Choose narrative tenses according to viewpoint, not event length alone.
Keep the subject of a shortened action clause clear.
Link experience to a proportionate recommendation for the intended readers.

sources.label: FEI TCF Canada: writing task 2 account with commentary, consulted 2026-09-07

sections.title: Choose a viewpoint, not a stopwatch rule
paragraphs: The imperfect presents a background, habit or situation viewed as ongoing. The `passé composé` presents an event as a completed whole or a turning point in the account. A long event can use the `passé composé`; a brief situation can use the imperfect. Duration alone does not choose the tense.

The pluperfect steps back before a past reference point. Return to the main sequence when that explanation is complete. Dates and connectors such as `au début`, `ensuite` and `finalement` help, but tense and logic must do the real work.
points: An account needs selected details that explain what changed, not a list of everything that happened.
`Un établi` (m.) is a workbench; `une consigne` (f.) is an instruction.

examples.french: Samedi, j'ai participé à un atelier de réparation de vélos. Il **pleuvait**, et plusieurs personnes attendaient près de l'entrée. J'**avais apporté** une vieille lampe, sans savoir si elle fonctionnait encore. Une bénévole m'a montré comment vérifier le contact, puis nous avons trouvé un fil desserré. Au début, je pensais qu'il fallait tout remplacer. Cette petite réparation m'a fait revoir mon jugement, sans me rendre capable de réparer n'importe quel appareil.
examples.english: On Saturday, I took part in a bicycle repair workshop. It was raining, and several people were waiting near the entrance. I had brought an old light, without knowing whether it still worked. A volunteer showed me how to check the contact, then we found a loose wire. At first, I thought everything needed replacing. This small repair made me reconsider my judgement without making me capable of repairing just any device.
examples.note: Background, prior preparation, main events and a limited conclusion work together. The technical detail is narrative context, not repair instructions.

examples.french: Nous **avons attendu** pendant une heure avant l'ouverture.
examples.english: We waited for an hour before opening time.
examples.note: A relatively long wait is presented as a completed episode.

examples.french: Quand la porte s'est ouverte, je **cherchais** encore mon message de confirmation.
examples.english: When the door opened, I was still looking for my confirmation message.
examples.note: The search is viewed in progress at the moment of opening.

mistakes.avoid: Quand je suis arrivé, l'atelier avait déjà commencer.
mistakes.prefer: Quand je suis arrivé, l'atelier avait déjà commencé.
mistakes.why: The pluperfect requires the past participle `commencé` after `avait`. It places the start before the arrival.

sections.title: Make causes and participants explicit
paragraphs: `Après avoir` + past participle presents an action completed before the main action. Its understood subject normally matches the main clause's subject. `En` + present participle, called the gerund, can express simultaneous action, means or cause; its subject should likewise be clear and ordinarily the same as that of the main verb.

`Parce que` states a cause. `Donc` presents a conclusion or consequence. `Pourtant` marks a result contrary to an expectation. Do not substitute them as decorative synonyms: the relationship between the facts decides. Use a full clause when a shortened one would make the wrong person act.
points: After an initial `en arrivant`, the subject that follows should be the person arriving.
An event occurring after another does not by itself prove that the earlier event caused it.

examples.french: **Après avoir observé** la démonstration, j'ai posé une question.
examples.english: After observing the demonstration, I asked a question.
examples.note: The observer and the questioner are both `je`.

examples.french: **En comparant** les deux pièces, nous avons repéré la différence.
examples.english: By comparing the two parts, we spotted the difference.
examples.note: The comparison is the means of discovering the difference; `nous` performs both actions.

examples.french: L'explication était courte ; **pourtant**, j'ai compris ce qu'il fallait faire.
examples.english: The explanation was short; nevertheless, I understood what needed to be done.
examples.note: The contrast implies that shortness might have made understanding harder in this context.

mistakes.avoid: En arrivant au centre, la porte était fermée.
mistakes.prefer: Quand je suis arrivé au centre, la porte était fermée.
mistakes.why: The shortened clause wrongly attaches arriving to `la porte`. A full clause explicitly names the person who arrived.

sections.title: Move from what happened to why readers should care
paragraphs: Commentary interprets an experience in relation to a purpose: recommending an event, explaining a difficulty or suggesting a change. One successful visit supports a personal observation, not proof that everyone will have the same experience. Signal the move with `cette expérience m'a montré` or `j'en retiens que`, then keep the conclusion proportionate.

A TCF Canada task 2 text is an account or narrative with relevant commentary, opinion or argument, in 120–150 words. The genre and audience may vary. The model below is an original community article for self-review, not an official exam response.
points: A recommendation should follow from the event you actually described.
A limitation can make a recommendation more useful, rather than cancelling it.

examples.french: **J'en retiens que** demander une explication peut être plus utile que deviner.
examples.english: What I take from it is that asking for an explanation can be more useful than guessing.
examples.note: `En` refers back to the experience; `peut` avoids a universal guarantee.

examples.french: Je recommanderais cet atelier aux débutants, **à condition de prévoir** assez de temps pour attendre son tour.
examples.english: I would recommend this workshop to beginners, provided they allow enough time to wait their turn.
examples.note: The account produces practical advice with a relevant condition.

practice.prompt: In the repair passage, what does il pleuvait contribute?
practice.explanation: The imperfect describes weather as background to the visit.

practice.prompt: Supply only apporter in the pluperfect: Avant l'atelier, j'___ une lampe.
practice.explanation: The prior action is formed with imperfect avoir and past participle apporté.

practice.prompt: Supply the required form of observer: Après avoir ___ la démonstration, j'ai essayé.
practice.explanation: Après avoir takes a past participle to express a completed prior action.

practice.prompt: Which conclusion stays within the evidence of one successful workshop visit?
choices: Tous les appareils sont faciles à réparer.
Cette visite m'a aidé à mieux comprendre un problème précis.
Je peux désormais tout réparer seul.
answers: Cette visite m'a aidé à mieux comprendre un problème précis.
practice.explanation: The conclusion is specific to the experience, not a claim of unlimited technical competence.

practice.prompt: Supply only attendre in the imperfect to present an action in progress: Quand l'annonce a retenti, nous ___ près du quai.
practice.explanation: The waiting is background already in progress when the announcement occurs.

practice.prompt: Supply only travailler in the passé composé for a completed whole: Hier, nous ___ toute la matinée à la préparation de la fête.
practice.explanation: A whole morning can be presented as one completed episode; long duration does not require the imperfect.

practice.prompt: Which sentence clearly makes the visitors, not the building, arrive?
choices: En arrivant, le bâtiment nous a surpris.
Quand nous sommes arrivés, le bâtiment nous a surpris.
answers: Quand nous sommes arrivés, le bâtiment nous a surpris.
practice.explanation: The full time clause gives arriving its own explicit subject.

practice.prompt: Use only the present participle of lire: En ___ la consigne, j'ai compris mon erreur.
practice.explanation: En lisant forms the gerund; je reads and understands.

practice.prompt: Supply only oublier in the pluperfect: Je n'ai pas pu montrer mon billet, car je l'___ chez moi.
practice.explanation: The earlier omission explains the later difficulty; billet is masculine singular.

practice.prompt: Choose the connector matching the stated contrast: Je connaissais bien le quartier ; ___, je me suis trompé de rue.
practice.explanation: Getting the street wrong contradicts the expectation created by knowing the neighbourhood.

practice.prompt: Join the actions using après avoir. Supply only the opening phrase, without a comma: Nous avons comparé les horaires, puis nous avons choisi un trajet.
practice.explanation: Both actions have nous as subject; the comparison is completed first.

practice.prompt: Read: J'ai trouvé l'accueil agréable, mais je n'ai assisté qu'à une séance. Copy the exact restriction starting with ne or its contracted form, without the final full stop.
practice.explanation: Only one session was observed, which limits the scope of the judgement.

practice.prompt: Supply only commencer in the past participle: La projection avait déjà ___ quand nous sommes entrés.
practice.explanation: The pluperfect marks a start preceding the arrival and requires a participle.

practice.prompt: An account says a visit was interesting but the room was crowded. Which recommendation uses both observations?
choices: La visite ne présente aucun intérêt.
Je conseille la visite, en prévoyant un moment moins fréquenté.
Il n'y a jamais personne dans cette salle.
answers: Je conseille la visite, en prévoyant un moment moins fréquenté.
practice.explanation: The recommendation preserves both interest and the practical limitation.

practice.prompt: Supply the two-word causal connector beginning with parce: Je suis revenu le lendemain ___ l'accueil était fermé.
practice.explanation: The closure is presented as the reason for returning another day.

practice.prompt: Use the exact opening taught for 'what I take from it', stopping before que: ___ que vérifier l'adresse évite des détours.
practice.explanation: J'en retiens que introduces a lesson drawn from the preceding experience.

production_task.prompt: Original situation: Write a 120–150-word article for your neighbourhood newsletter about your first visit to a tool-lending workshop. Include the setting, an initial difficulty, what changed and a useful recommendation with a limitation. Invent a plausible personal experience, not statistics or technical safety advice. Self-review only.
production_task.model_answer: Samedi dernier, j'ai découvert l'atelier de prêt d'outils du quartier. Il y avait du monde, et je ne savais pas à qui m'adresser. J'avais préparé une liste de petits travaux, mais j'avais oublié de noter les dimensions nécessaires. Une bénévole m'a alors expliqué comment choisir le matériel en fonction du projet, sans me pousser à emprunter tout de suite. Après avoir discuté avec elle, j'ai décidé de rentrer mesurer mon étagère avant de revenir. Cette visite ne m'a donc pas permis de commencer immédiatement mes travaux, mais elle m'a évité un choix précipité. Je recommande cet atelier aux personnes qui souhaitent poser des questions avant d'emprunter. Prévoyez toutefois du temps pour l'échange et arrivez avec une description précise de votre projet : l'accueil sera plus utile pour vous comme pour les bénévoles.
production_task.translation: Last Saturday, I discovered the neighbourhood tool-lending workshop. It was busy, and I did not know whom to approach. I had prepared a list of small jobs, but I had forgotten to note the necessary dimensions. A volunteer then explained how to choose equipment according to the project, without pushing me to borrow immediately. After talking with her, I decided to go home and measure my shelf before returning. So this visit did not allow me to start work immediately, but it saved me from a hasty choice. I recommend this workshop to people who want to ask questions before borrowing. However, allow time for the conversation and arrive with a precise description of your project: the assistance will be more useful both for you and for the volunteers.
rubric: I distinguish background, earlier preparation and the events that advance the account.
The subject of `après avoir` or `en` + participle is clear; connectors express the intended relationship.
My commentary follows from the experience and gives readers a useful, proportionate recommendation.
I check 120–150 words, audience and readability. This free-writing task remains self-review rather than an automatically assessed language level.
